correctness.rationale: The explicit assumptions and transition probabilities specify two independent draws from the n−1 other agents, with repeats allowed; the Finding's phrase 'distinct-index neighbors' should not be read as excluding repeats. At bias 1/9 the exact up/down ratio gives r=8k(n−k)/[(n−1)²+8k²]. The first-step differences satisfy λ_k d_k−μ_k d_(k−1)=1 and the initial equation at k=0, with absorption and finite mean guaranteed by the finite positive upward path. Iteration and summation give exactly the two nested sums. For x=k/n, 1−f(x)=(4x−1)²/(1+8x²), and the log perturbation from excluding the updater is O(1/n). At width h=n^(2/3), λ→1/8 and summing log r produces −(32/9)(u³−v³); the O(h/n) perturbation disappears. Globally the product is bounded by a constant times exp[−c n^(−2)Σ(ℓ−n/4)²]. The block of m successive indices has sum of squares at least (m³−m)/12. When the right endpoint is far from n/4, the terms with m≤|k−n/4|/2 have the extra decay exp[−c m(k−n/4)²/n²], and the rest have the cubic tail. With λ bounded below for k≤n/2 these give the integrable O(h/[1+((k−n/4)/h)²]) bound on d_k. The last half is O(n log n) by a fixed ratio gap starting at 3n/8, with earlier-index products suppressed. These estimates justify the inner and outer limits, including all fixed starts below 1/4, and the Gaussian midpoint integration gives the stated Gamma(1/6) coefficient. At p>1/4 one can start the ratio gap at a fixed p0 strictly between 1/4 and p, not at p itself. For k≥(1−δ)n, terms beginning below (1−2δ)n are exponentially suppressed, the remaining ratios are O(δ), and 1/λ_k=(n/(n−k))[1+O(δ+1/n)]. Hence the final states give coefficient 1 in front of n log n as δ→0, and the earlier states are O_δ(n). The scale counts individual updates throughout.
residual_risks: The claim is an expectation limit at the exact bias, not a weak limit of the hitting time or a bias-detuning theorem. Finite rational tests are consistency checks only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither stated theorem handles the exact discrete quadratic bottleneck with far-left starts and absorption near the upper boundary; convergence on a stopped bounded diffusion window would not itself give mean hitting time to consensus.

evidence: The local generator inferred from the transition probabilities is (1/8)∂²+(4/3)u²∂, so the generic diffusion passage formula does give F and C once convergence of the means is established.

The original neighbor-only finite-n terms alter log ratios by O(1/n); controlling their sum over O(n^(2/3)) and bounding contributions from all other states is required. The coarse off-critical conclusions supply neither of these nor the harmonic endpoint coefficient at equality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The noncovered result is a discrete limit and matching theorem, not extraction of a new constant from a known continuous passage formula. Simple substitution into the off-critical bounds or the saddle-node ODE does not establish it.

Hathcock–Sethna Eq. (14) is the very same double integral for the diffusion with V(u)=−4u³/9 and noise amplitude 1/2, using start s and sending the absorbing point to +∞; Eq. (15) supplies the full-line passage value in Airy form.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This recognizes mathematical equivalence of the limiting integral rather than claiming a new saddle-node function. Diffusion normalization alone is not a theorem transferring expected total consensus time of the discrete finite chain to that integral.

originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the controlled discrete consensus asymptotic for the original neighbor-only chain: critical-window start profile, below-window matching and above-window n log n matching at the precise bias omitted in the same-model prior theorem. The cubic diffusion kernel and its full-passage constant in saddle-node units are classical; only their rigorously derived realization and normalization in this chain, plus matching to actual consensus, are credited. Neither the same-model off-critical bounds nor the diffusion calculation implies the required uniform integrability or the remote absorbing-end estimate.
residual_risks: A general birth–death saddle-node passage theorem with suitable global matching hypotheses could narrow the contribution; the checked Langevin result is not such a theorem. Bounded searches do not exclude uncataloged model-specific work.

value.rationale: The exact threshold is a natural gap between fast and exponentially slow regimes. The result identifies a different scale, quantifies the dependence on starts across the bottleneck, and separates it from a distinct coupon-collector endpoint even at the same bias. This is useful discrete finite-size information about a standard model beyond the known continuous normal form.
residual_risks: The work does not address the absorption-time distribution, general graphs or a detuned bias window.
